selection_bias_against_the_goal_s_own_ta.mechanism: The dominant tier (event_id_echo, 93.6% of all matches) finds an event precisely because its recall_event_id was written into the transcript, and the main reason an id gets written there is the memory_remember provenance that CONSUMES it. That tier is therefore close to a consumption detector rather than a neutral join. The one tier with no such coupling, transport_session, shows a consumed share of 0.182 — essentially the store-wide base rate of 0.172 — and it recovers only 434 events (0.73% of the store).

recency_confound_ruled_out.conclusion: The enrichment holds inside every month, so it is not a recency artifact of which transcripts survive on disk.
recency_confound_ruled_out.test: consumed share compared between matched and unmatched events within each calendar month

selection_bias_against_the_goal_s_own_ta.why_this_matters: Phase 2 exists to grade SILENT (non-consumed) recalls. The join recovers 2398 silent events = 4.06% of the store, and selects them by a mechanism correlated with the very outcome variable phase 4 would model. Grading this sample would yield a distribution over a biased, unrepresentative 4%, and a replay A/B trained on it could not support the pre-registered generalization claim.

structural_ceiling.implication: Even a flawless join over the transcripts that still exist could not exceed ~12.6% coverage. The 60% falsifier is unreachable on this corpus, so the failure is structural — not a defect of the runner, and not fixable by tuning join tiers.
